hero.headline: A Navigator for Families in ICE Detention Situations
hero.subheadline: An organized, step-by-step tool to help families navigate the ICE detention process — available in Russian and English.
hero.disclaimer_inline: Informational tool only. Not a law firm.

modules.heading: Three modules to help you get organized

navigator.title: Crisis Navigator
navigator.description: An 8-step checklist organized into three phases. Helps families manage immediate priorities: locating the detained person, establishing communication, and beginning document collection.

evidence.title: Evidence Builder
evidence.description: A secure document storage system to upload and organize records by category and year — the format attorneys commonly request.

monitor.title: Status Monitor
monitor.description: Automated tracking of changes in the ICE detainee locator and EOIR system. Alerts when changes are detected.

three_rules_promo.heading: Three Rules — Free, Always
three_rules_promo.text: The Three Rules page is available without registration or payment. It contains general information about what detained individuals commonly do and avoid — published by immigrant rights organizations.

items.question: Is this legal advice?
items.answer: No. Detention Navigator is an informational tool only. It helps organize information and documents, but is not a substitute for a licensed immigration attorney. If you need legal help, please contact an attorney.

items.question: Is my data safe?
items.answer: Yes. All data is stored in encrypted form. The A-Number is encrypted using AES-256-GCM before being written to the database. Only you have access to your data. We do not share or sell data to third parties.

items.question: Does this work for facilities outside California?
items.answer: Yes. While some facility database information is California-focused (primarily Adelanto), the tool works for any ICE facility. The checklist structure and document logic are universal.

items.question: How do I find an attorney?
items.answer: The Navigator includes a step on finding an attorney with information on how to verify a license and avoid fraud. For free legal help: ilrc.org or ailalawyer.com.

footer.tagline: Informational tool only. Not a law firm, not a substitute for an attorney.
